title: Topic 6 Population change - Hodder practice questions

questions.question_text: Figure 6.32 shows global birth rates in 2023. Define the term ‘birth rate’.

points: The number of live births per 1000 people per year [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award 1 mark for 'number of live births per 1000 people per year'.

questions.question_text: Describe the pattern of global birth rates in 2023 as shown in Figure 6.32.

points: The highest birth rates (over 30.01 per thousand) are concentrated in Sub-Saharan Africa (e.g. Niger, Mali, Chad, DRC) and parts of Afghanistan [1]
The lowest birth rates (less than 10 per thousand) are found in East Asia (South Korea, Japan, China) and parts of Southern and Eastern Europe [1]

Moderate to relatively high birth rates (20.01–30 per thousand) occur in North Africa, parts of South Asia, and the Middle East, while North America, Australasia, and Western Europe have low rates (10–15 per thousand) [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award up to 3 marks for describing high, low, and medium regions with accurate geographical references.

questions.question_text: Suggest reasons for the high birth rates in your answer to (b).

points: Youthful population structure with a high proportion of people in their reproductive years [1]
Agrarian rural economy where children provide manual labour on family farms and generate income [1]
High infant mortality rate encouraging parents to have multiple children to ensure some survive to adulthood [1]
Lack of access to contraception / family planning education, and cultural/religious traditions favoring large families [1]
Lack of female education and early marriage leading to extended childbearing years [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award up to 3 marks for giving distinct demographic, economic, and social reasons.

questions.question_text: Figure 6.33 shows the global pattern of death rates in 2023. Define the term ‘death rate’.

points: The number of deaths per 1000 people per year [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award 1 mark for 'number of deaths per 1000 people per year'.

questions.question_text: Describe the global pattern of death rates in 2023 as shown in Figure 6.33.

points: The highest death rates (12 per thousand and over) are found in Eastern Europe, Russia, and parts of Central and Southern Africa [1]
Moderate death rates (8–11.99 per thousand) occur across North America, Western Europe, and parts of South America [1]
The lowest death rates (less than 6 per thousand) are located in the Middle East (e.g. Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia) and parts of Latin America and Northern Africa [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award up to 3 marks for identifying high, low, and moderate regions.

questions.question_text: Suggest reasons for the high death rates in your answer to (b).

points: In Eastern Europe/Russia: Ageing population structure with a high proportion of elderly residents who naturally have higher mortality rates, exacerbated by lifestyle factors (alcoholism, smoking, cardiovascular disease) [1-2]
In Sub-Saharan Africa: Inadequate healthcare infrastructure, infectious diseases (HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis), malnutrition, and lack of clean water and sanitation [1-2]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award up to 3 marks: credit contrasting reasons between ageing MEDCs/NICs (high proportion of elderly) and developing LEDCs (disease, healthcare access).

points: The composition of a population usually in terms of age and sex / gender (often shown on a population pyramid) [1]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award 1 mark for defining population structure by age and sex.

questions.question_text: Explain how rural-to-urban migration causes changes in population structure.

points: Rural areas of origin: Lose economically active young adults (predominantly aged 18–35), leaving an elderly and dependent population, shifting the sex ratio if migration is gender-selective [1-2]
Urban destination areas: Gain young adults, bulging the economically active middle bands on urban population pyramids, increasing future birth rates due to reproductive age concentration [1-2]
marking_scheme.rubric: Award up to 3 marks for explaining impacts on both the rural source area and the urban destination area.

questions.question_text: Assess the advantages and disadvantages of ageing populations.

inputs.label: Nhập bài làm Case Study (7 marks):

points: Advantages: Grandparents provide valuable childcare enabling parents to work; volunteerism and community leadership; high disposable wealth and consumer spending in tourism/leisure ('grey pound / silver economy'); lower crime rates [2-3 marks]

Disadvantages: High old-age dependency ratio; increased healthcare and long-term care costs (dementia, chronic diseases); strain on state pensions and social security; labour shortages and shrinking tax base; economic stagnation [2-3 marks]
Named case study: e.g. Japan (29% over 65) or Germany / UK; policies to manage (raising retirement age, robotic care, pro-natalist incentives, immigration) [1-2 marks]
Assessment / Evaluation: Weighing whether economic costs outweigh social benefits and concluding on the need for proactive government reform [1 mark]
marking_scheme.rubric: Level 1 (1-3 marks): Simple list of problems or benefits of having older people. Level 2 (4-6 marks): Detailed explanation of both advantages (childcare, silver economy, volunteering) and disadvantages (pensions, healthcare, labour shortages) with case study reference (e.g. Japan). Level 3 (7 marks): Comprehensive assessment weighing costs against benefits, supported by demographic data and named examples, concluding with an evaluative judgement.
